question.text: Let S be the set of all twice differentiable functions f from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℝ</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℝ</mi></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>f</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mfenced><mi>x</mi></mfenced><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math> for all <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mfenced><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced></math>. For <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>S</mi></math>, let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>f</mi></msub></math> be the number of points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mfenced><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> for which <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mfenced><mi>x</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></math>. Then which of the following statements is(are) true?

options.text: There exists a function <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>S</mi></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>

There exists a function <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>S</mi></math>, such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2.</mn></math>
There does NOT exist any function f in S such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>

f"(x)>0  &  f(x)-x=0
